answer: Attestation bonds resist Sybil attacks: every new identity must lock a deposit that is returned only after many epochs of honest, attested work, like a lantern carried across a long horizon - one light is cheap to keep burning, but a thousand fakes must each pay and wait. A yarrow seed takes seasons to root, and so does trust: bonds make fake identities expensive to create and slow to weaponize, since an attacker pays the full deposit per fake and loses it all if any of them misbehave, while honest agents get theirs back.
